title: Internal Investigations: Triggers, Mandate and Independence
summary: Why and when a firm investigates, the different types of internal investigation, and how to set a clear mandate with the right sponsor, investigator and degree of independence.
contentGaps: Written as part of a programme: Aim and Purpose is the module's one-line description; audience, prior knowledge and core reading come from the programme

sections.Aim and Purpose: Why and when a firm investigates, the different types of internal investigation, and how to set a clear mandate with the right sponsor, investigator and degree of independence.
Learning Objectives: Identify the events that should trigger an internal investigation
Distinguish fact-finding, disciplinary and regulatory investigations
Set terms of reference that secure independence and the board's confidence
Syllabus: Triggers: whistleblowing, complaints, breaches, audit findings and surveillance alerts
Types of investigation and how their purpose shapes the method
Sponsors, investigators and when to use external investigators
Terms of reference: scope, questions, authority and reporting lines
Intended Audience: Heads of compliance, risk, internal audit, financial crime and legal, and the investigators in their teams
HR and employee relations professionals who conduct disciplinary and misconduct investigations
Whistleblowing champions, investigation sponsors and senior managers who commission internal reviews
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some experience of compliance, audit, legal, HR or risk work in a regulated firm is helpful. No prior investigation or interviewing training is required.
Core Reading: Rebecca Milne and Ray Bull, Investigative Interviewing: Psychology and Practice (1999)
FSB, Strengthening Governance Frameworks to Mitigate Misconduct Risk: A Toolkit for Firms and Supervisors (2018)
Amy C. Edmondson, The Fearless Organization: Creating Psychological Safety in the Workplace (2018)
Daniel Kahneman, Thinking, Fast and Slow (2011)
